item.title: Runa Laila is alive and well, says angry daughter amid death rumours
item.description:
Tani Laila, the only daughter of renowned singer Runa Laila, has expressed anger over the circulation of a report and an AI-generated video claiming that the legendary singer is 'battling for her life'.

She said her mother, Runa Laila, is completely healthy and alive. She also said the videos and images circulating on social media are not authentic and were created using AI.

Tani Laila, who is currently living in the United States with her family, expressed her frustration in a social media post.

She said she is irritated and fed up with people creating such posts, AI-generated YouTube videos and spreading false news in an attempt to make a small amount of money.

Tani said she would personally start reporting such content. She also urged people to take action against such accounts one by one.

The spread of false reports about her musician mother’s death is particularly distressing for Tani. Runa Laila has earned the love of countless people through six decades in music. Her daughter believes that spreading such a sensitive false report about the legendary singer is disrespectful to the family.

Tani wrote, “My mother is completely healthy and alive; no one has died, nor is anyone on the verge of death. These are all AI-generated videos and images.”

Tani also urged news media to exercise caution. She requested that they verify information and exercise due care before publishing or broadcasting any report about Runa Laila.

Expressing her anger over the rumours about her mother’s death, Tani said, “She is alive! This is becoming unbearable.”

She also urged people who follow Runa Laila to report such accounts.

Meanwhile, Runa Laila has remained active in musical events in recent months. Last month, she performed at two concerts in two Australian states. Before that, she performed at a solo musical event organised by Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy. She has also selectively taken part in several other stage programmes.

item.title: SSC re-evaluation results tomorrow, how to check
item.description:
The results of the re-evaluation of the SSC and equivalent examinations 2026 will be published tomorrow, on Thursday.

The results will be published on the education boards’ websites at around 10am.

The Inter-Education Board Examination Controllers’ Committee said this in a notice issued on Wednesday.

According to the notice, the re-evaluation results can be accessed in three ways. First, the results will be published on the respective education boards’ websites. Second, applicants will receive the results by SMS on the mobile phone numbers they provided. The results can also be accessed through the website rescrutiny.eduboardresults.gov.bd.

More than 400,000 candidates have submitted nearly 1.3 million applications for re-evaluation of their results in this year’s Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and equivalent examinations.

Of these, more than 1.056 million applications were submitted for answer scripts of the written or theoretical examinations, while more than 231,000 applications were submitted for practical examinations.

This year, the answer scripts will be re-evaluated as part of the re-evaluation process. Under the education boards’ previous rules, there was no provision for re-evaluating answer scripts. The boards would only check whether there had been any errors in adding or deducting marks when reviewing the answer scripts of applicants.

The education boards are now under pressure as they have to re-evaluate and review a large number of answer scripts. Asked about the matter, Professor Syed Akhtaruzzaman, president of the Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee and chairman of the Dhaka Education Board, told Prothom Alo that answer scripts would be re-evaluated this year. As a result, the boards have had to appoint the required number of examiners. There is no alternative, he said.

The SSC and equivalent examination results were published on 10 August. After maintaining relatively high pass rates for many years, SSC results have declined somewhat over the past two years. This year, the pass rate among the nine general education boards fell to 64.05 per cent, the lowest in 19 years. It was also lower than the previous year. The number of students securing GPA-5 also fell by nearly 19,000.

The combined average pass rate across the nine general education boards, Madrasa Education Board and Technical Education Board stood at 62.25 per cent this year. This means nearly 38 per cent of candidates failed to pass. More than 1.829 million candidates took the examinations this year. The decline in the pass rate has naturally drawn considerable attention, which has also been reflected in the number of applications for re-evaluation.

Applications for re-evaluation were accepted online from 11 August to 17 August. According to education board sources, 402,051 candidates under the 11 education boards submitted a total of 1,287,926 applications for re-evaluation of their answer scripts. Of these, 1,056,455 applications were for written examinations and 231,471 for practical examinations.

Dhaka Education Board Senior System Analyst Manzurul Kabir recently told Prothom Alo that 94,236 candidates under the board had submitted 277,665 applications for written examinations and 58,012 applications for practical examinations.

A review of data from the other education boards showed that Dhaka recorded the highest number of applications. More than 35,000 candidates applied in Cumilla, over 39,000 in Rajshahi, more than 28,000 in Jashore, over 39,000 in Chattogram, more than 17,000 in Barishal, over 20,000 in Sylhet, more than 37,000 in Dinajpur and 27,676 in Mymensingh for re-evaluation of results in one or more subjects.

More than 40,000 candidates under the Madrasa Education Board and over 20,000 under the Technical Education Board also applied for re-evaluation.

item.title: TOP SHOTS (9 September 2026)
What is the secret behind Hasan’s success at Kent?
item.description:
Hasan Mahmud is now Kent’s “poster boy”. He has not played many matches, and the Bangladesh pace bowler is currently featuring in only his fourth game for the English county club. Yet that has been enough to make an impact. Hasan has now become the team’s main bowling threat.

He was once again the team’s best bowler against Derbyshire yesterday, Tuesday. Hasan bowled 15.5 overs, conceded just 30 runs and claimed a team-high four wickets.

How is Hasan producing his best in these unfamiliar conditions? What was his bowling plan against Derbyshire yesterday, Tuesday? The answer lies in Hasan’s own words, published on Kent Cricket’s website. Speaking about his bowling, Hasan said, “On a new wicket, my plan was to focus on hitting the right length and conceding as few runs as possible.”

His figures clearly show that Hasan managed to execute that plan. He bowled almost 16 overs and conceded fewer than two runs per over on average. Hasan was not the only Bangladeshi representative to impress for Kent on Tuesday. Khaled Ahmed also made an immediate impact, taking three wickets on his county debut for Kent.

Hasan and Khaled were effectively Kent’s two best bowlers against Derbyshire yesterday. Their excellent bowling helped bowl Derbyshire out for 300 in the first innings on their home ground.

Hasan also expressed his delight at Khaled’s performance.

“I was certainly pleased to have Khaled alongside me as a bowling partner. I am very happy for him. He took three wickets in his first match for Kent. Hopefully, he will do well in the next innings as well.”

Hasan has also noticed how pleased Bangladesh supporters are to see two of their compatriots playing for Kent. He said, “People in Bangladesh are also very happy that two of us are playing for Kent. Especially after what happened in Australia, this has become even more special for us.”

Surely, you know the story of what happened in Australia!

item.title: DUCSU lags in fulfilling promises, leaders caught in controversy
item.description:
Before the Dhaka University Central Students' Union (DUCSU) elections, the Islami Chhatra Shibir-backed panel "Oikkoboddho Shikkarthi Jote" (United Students' Alliance) had pledged to ensure legitimate seat allocations in the residential halls for every student from their first year. However, that promise has not been fulfilled.

Shafinur Rahman Tazim, a student of Amar Ekushey Hall from the 2025-26 academic session at Dhaka University, started his classes in April. Although nearly five months have passed, he has still not been allocated a seat in the hall.

"Since I didn't get a seat in my hall, I have to live in rented accommodation outside. This involves higher expenses as well as greater suffering," Shafinur said.

Today marks one year since the DUCSU elections. The voting for DUCSU was held on this day in 2025, where the Chhatra Shibir-backed Oikkoboddho Shikkarthi Jote (United Students' Alliance) panel won most of the posts. One year later, it appears that very few of DUCSU’s key promises regarding accommodation crises, food quality, campus safety and other critical areas have been fulfilled.

On the other hand, rival student organizations allege that DUCSU leaders have been involved in controversies more often than they have delivered on their promises.

Before the election, the panel had opposed subservient student politics, but DUCSU Vice-President (VP) Shadik Kayem himself later engaged in party-subservient politics with Jamaat-e-Islami and took part in the party’s election campaign. Some DUCSU leaders have also faced allegations of taking the law into their own hands and mobilising mob violence, among other controversies.

Some students and teachers of Dhaka university say that Islami Chhatra Shibir activists had previously interfered in students’ personal freedom in various ways at campuses under their control. Such incidents have not been seen to the same extent during DUCSU’s one-year tenure. There have also been no incidents of occupying halls or violent clashes over hall control. Classes and examinations were held smoothly. In this regard, the role of Chhatra Dal was also significant, as they were not seen attempting to occupy halls like before.

Tanzimuddin Khan, a professor of international relations at Dhaka University told Prothom Alo that there is no denying that some changes had taken place because of electoral politics. But it remains to be seen how long these changes can be sustained.

July, DUCSU polls and the aftermath

Dhaka University campus had historically been dominated by the student wing of the ruling party. For fifteen and a half years prior to July 2024, it was under the control of the now banned Chhatra League.

Chhatra League would allocate a large number of rooms in the halls to students of its choice. Those who did not meet its preferences were forced to leave. Forcing students to attend political processions and torturing them in the name of teaching manners in the hall guestrooms were common practices. Organising rallies and processions in support of the government and the Awami League and suppressing protests were the primary activities of Chhatra League on campus.

During the anti-discrimination student movement in July 2024, students drove Chhatra League activists out of the halls. After the fall of the Awami League government, the university administration took control of the halls. However, many leaders of Chhatra Dal and left-leaning student organisations alleged that monitoring teams, environment teams and other groups were formed at the time to exert influence over the administration. They claimed that many of those leading these committees were Chhatra Shibir activists posing as general students.

Prior to the July mass uprising, Chhatra Shibir was unable to carry out politics at Dhaka University. Following the uprising, Chhatra Shibir was able to establish its political presence on campus. At the same time, demands to ban subservient student politics grew stronger. General students demanded that such politics should not return to Dhaka University.

Against this backdrop, Chhatra Dal announced convening committees for the university’s halls in August 2025, triggering protests. The decision to keep student politics banned in the halls was subsequently upheld. Earlier, during the July uprising, hall authorities had banned student politics in the halls under pressure from students.

Chhatra Dal, however, alleged that Chhatra Shibir had orchestrated the protests in the name of general students to prevent Chhatra Dal from carrying out organisational activities in the halls. The party described it as a political manoeuvre.

In the DUCSU election held on 9 September, 2025, Shibir-backed panel won 23 of the 28 posts. Shadik Kayem became vice-president (VP), while SM Farhad became general secretary (GS). Chhatra Shibir-backed panels also won student union elections across five universities, not just Dhaka University.

In forming their panel, Shibir adopted a strategy of demonstrating diversity by including ethnic minorities and women.

How far was the manifesto fulfilled

The Chhatra Shibir-backed panel had promised 36 reforms within 12 months. DUCSU VP Shadik Kayem and GS SM Farhad told Prothom Alo that initiatives had been taken to implement all the commitments mentioned in the manifesto. They said, however, that not all the work could be completed because they did not receive adequate cooperation from the administration.

Shadik Kayem told Prothom Alo on 17 August that instead of asking the university for funds, they had only sought permission for their initiatives. Even at that level, he said, they had not received sufficient cooperation.

But Dhaka University Treasurer Professor M Jahangir Alam Chowdhury rejected the allegation. He told Prothom Alo that DUCSU had received more funds than the amount allocated to it.

Prothom Alo sent Shadik Kayem a list of the 36 manifesto commitments and asked how many had been fulfilled. According to his response, various committees had been formed and the hall unions had been conducting regular monitoring to ensure hygienic food for students. To address the accommodation crisis, a project worth Tk 28.41 billion had been inaugurated as part of a long-term plan. New buses had been arranged to ensure safe transport for female students, maternity leave had been introduced, online payment had been launched for the admission process, common rooms had been renovated, new resources had been added to the central library, a skill development summit had been organised and the university medical centre had been modernised. The number of bus trips had also been increased, while various halls had started providing free hygiene products to female students, among other initiatives.

Some students, however, say the Chhatra Shibir-backed panel has failed to bring sustainable and lasting changes in the areas covered by its manifesto. Food quality remains largely unchanged. The campus is still not safe, with incidents of mob violence repeatedly taking place. There has also been little progress in reducing students’ difficulties at the Registrar Building.

Food quality remains one of the biggest problems for Dhaka University students and was one of the key priorities in the manifesto. There was increased monitoring for some time after the DUCSU election and the initiative received considerable publicity. However, worms, razor blades and cockroaches have recently been found in food served at the canteens of several halls.

Tasfian Ahmed, a student from the 2023–24 academic session, told Prothom Alo, ‘They raised demands and held meetings, then publicised those efforts as their own initiatives. But the students’ problems were not solved. Can that really be called fulfilment of the manifesto?’

The 36-point manifesto contained several specific commitments concerning female students. Work has been undertaken on breastfeeding rooms, childcare corners, safe transport and self-defence training. The deadline for female students to enter the halls has also been extended by one hour. However, some commitments, including access to halls for non-resident female students, appointing female staff in all common rooms and setting up guardian lounges in the halls, have not been implemented.

Before the DUCSU election, the panel had pledged to create a safe campus for women. But there has been little progress on this front, according to Prionti, a student of Samsunnahar Hall. Israt Jahan, another student of the same hall, said she returns to the hall after tutoring at night. On her way back, she often encounters drug users and vagrants who frequently harass female students.

‘If you are afraid even while moving around the campus, how can it be called a safe campus?’ she said.

Mounting controversies

Although there had been a movement at Dhaka University against subservient student politics, Shadik Kayem and Assistant General Secretary Mohiuddin Khan took part in Jamaat-e-Islami’s election campaign during the national election. Jamaat has also named Shadik Kayem as its candidate for the Dhaka South City Corporation election. This has raised questions about whether Chhatra Shibir has actually stayed away from subservient politics.

Several DUCSU leaders have been involved in various controversies, including alleged abuse of power in the name of eviction drives, forcing children who went to play on fields to perform sit-ups while holding their ears, harassing an Awami League-backed teacher, distributing cigarettes at a concert, distorting the history of the Liberation War, arguing with transgender people and having only three people present at the National Martyrs’ Memorial on Independence Day.

Nahiduzzaman Shipon, general secretary of the Dhaka University unit of Chhatra Dal, told Prothom Alo that before the DUCSU election, Chhatra Shibir’s panel had tried to portray itself as neutral and non-partisan. ‘Immediately after the election, DUCSU began implementing Jamaat’s agenda,’ he said.

Is there a culture of fear

Some believe that the most important indicators for assessing the state of a university are whether there is a culture of fear, academic freedom and space for free thought and freedom of expression.

Professor Tanzimuddin Khan believes that the authoritarian political culture and culture of fear against which the mass uprising took place have returned following the DUCSU election.

Referring to tendencies such as exerting undue influence over university administration decisions, creating mobs, taking the law into one’s own hands and attaching various negative labels to opponents, Tanzimuddin Khan said that there were times when it was difficult to find any difference between the methods used by some DUCSU leaders and those previously used by Chhatra League leaders, now banned.

Teachers and students believe that DUCSU elections must be held regularly to preserve whatever positive changes have taken place. The DUCSU election was held in 2025 after a six-year gap following the previous election in 2019. Before that, an election had been held 25 years ago, in 1990.

DUCSU’s term will end on 14 September. If no election is held, its term will be extended by three months. If an election is still not held during that period, the current student union will be dissolved.

Asked whether an election would be held, Dhaka University Vice-Chancellor Professor ABM Obaidul Islam told Prothom Alo, ‘The DUCSU election should certainly be held. It must be held.’

Despite the vice-chancellor’s assurances, doubts remain among many. This is because political governments have generally been reluctant to allow DUCSU elections to take place.

item.title: “I still carry that trauma”: 45 accounts of childhood sexual abuse shared on new platform in 24 hours
item.description:
Most of the victims were between the ages of seven and 12 when the abuse occurred. Sixty-three per cent said they had been abused more than once, while 38 per cent said the abuse continued over an extended period—initially through force and later through threats.

These findings have emerged from a new platform called awaz.bd. The platform has been created to document accounts of sexual abuse suffered during childhood. Within 24 hours of its launch at 4:00 pm on 7 September, 45 people had shared harrowing accounts of their experiences during childhood.

The platform was initially intended primarily to document cases of sexual abuse of boys. However, girls have also written about being sexually abused during their childhood.

Upon entering the platform, the words ‘Awaz Uthao’ (Raise Your Voice) appear on the screen, alongside the message: “Your silence encourages crime; your information helps combat crime.”

It also states that the statistics have been compiled from information submitted by people anonymously to help understand the true scale of child abuse in Bangladesh, particularly in educational institutions. No names, photographs or identifying information are included. No cookies or tracking are used, and none of the information submitted will be stored.

Why this platform

The platform was primarily developed by Rakibul Hasan, 27, and Salahuddin Jahangir, 42.

Rakibul Hasan graduated in international relations from Dhaka University and now works as an online entrepreneur. Salahuddin Jahangir is pursuing an MPhil at Islamic University in Kushtia and works for a private organisation.

Rakibul Hasan told Prothom Alo on Tuesday that they took the initiative to create such a platform after a number of cases of rape of boys, particularly at madrasahs, came to light.

He said they were inspired by the “Ghus” website. Just as the Ghus site generated a response among the public and reached policymakers within the government, the aim of the new platform was to ensure that cases of child abuse would similarly prompt the government to take notice, he said.

Among educational institutions, including religious institutions, 56 per cent of the reported cases occurred at Qawmi madrasahs and 19 per cent at schools. Alia madrasahs, mosques and universities were also mentioned.

“This is not a help centre or a legal assistance centre. It is an awareness platform,” Rakibul Hasan added.

Rakibul Hasan further said he had studied at a Qawmi madrasah and therefore had first-hand experience of madrasah culture.

“We want the government and madrasah boards to take active steps to stop sexual abuse of children in madrasahs. We want awaz.bd to create social pressure on the government to take action,” he said.

Describing the response since the platform was launched as unprecedented, Rakibul Hasan said they had initially intended to document only cases of abuse of boys at madrasahs.

However, people from all types of educational institutions, both men and women, had responded to the platform. Victims have shared their experiences of sexual abuse during childhood and offered advice to others on how to stay aware, he said.

More victims abused by relatives at home

One man shared an account of being abused during childhood, writing: “This happened to me many times in my life. Initially, my own cousin raped me in our own home. There were times when he did it every day. At first, I did not understand what was happening. Later, when I came to understand, I became involved in it myself. And to be honest, these things do not happen only in madrasahs. As far as I know, many people are currently involved in this heinous practice.”

One person wrote in the platformThere needs to be very close monitoring of such matters in all residential institutions. Why should innocent childhoods be ruined at the hands of such inhuman people? If a madrasah or school cannot ensure children’s complete safety, why should anyone have the courage to open one?

A woman wrote about being sexually abused while she was in Class-V: “One of my maternal cousins used to come to our house to tutor me. He would sometimes play cricket with us in the courtyard or on the veranda... One day, when my mother was not at home, he took me to my room on the pretext of playing another game... Even now, I shudder whenever I remember these things...”

The platform has presented the 45 accounts statistically. Separate data have been provided for male and female victims, showing that 64 per cent of the victims were male.

Among boys, 32 per cent of the abuse was perpetrated by acquaintances, 26 per cent by trusted acquaintances, 16 per cent by close relatives and 10 per cent by more distant relatives. Among girls, 7 per cent of cases involved acquaintances, 14 per cent trusted acquaintances, 14 per cent close relatives and 43 per cent more distant relatives. Some cases also involved strangers and others.

One in five victims was abused by a family member while 56 per cent of the abuse occurred at home. Of these, 54 per cent took place in the victim’s own home, 19 per cent in the alleged perpetrator’s home and 15 per cent at the home of the victim’s relatives.

Alarming scale of abuse in educational institutions

One person wrote, “At the time, I studied at one of the country’s well-known Qawmi madrasahs. The room next to ours was where the older students lived. ...One day I had a very high fever. I was asleep. Suddenly, I realised that someone’s hand was inside my pyjamas. Then, out of fear, I opened my eyes slightly and saw that older student.”

“There needs to be very close monitoring of such matters in all residential institutions. Why should innocent childhoods be ruined at the hands of such inhuman people? If a madrasah or school cannot ensure children’s complete safety, why should anyone have the courage to open one?” the person added.

Another person wrote, “I studied at a kindergarten school in a village. The head teacher also tutored us privately. Several of us would stay at school at night so that we could do well in our studies. During that time, I was abused several times by an older student. I still carry that trauma today.”

According to the platform’s statistics, 36 per cent of respondents said they had been sexually abused at educational institutions.

Rakibul Hasan, one of two developers of the siteWe want the government and madrasah boards to take active steps to stop sexual abuse of children in madrasahs. We want awaz.bd to create social pressure on the government to take action.

Among educational institutions, including religious institutions, 56 per cent of the reported cases occurred at Qawmi madrasahs and 19 per cent at schools. Alia madrasahs, mosques and universities were also mentioned.

Some respondents wrote that being abused as children can lead victims to become abusers themselves.

One man wrote, “When I was growing up at my maternal grandparents’ home, a maternal cousin who lived nearby would sometimes take me into the woods and do bad things to me. When I grew a little older, a school friend would also do similar things whenever he got the opportunity. To be honest, it was so terrible, so horrifying, that it is beyond imagination! Later, after seeing what they did, I too became involved in such acts.”

Some respondents also stressed the need for parents to remain vigilant to protect children from abuse.

One woman wrote: “I feel sick to my stomach. A few animals have destroyed my life. ...My maternal cousin was the first. At my grandparents’ home, he did something to me under the pretext of playing and told me not to tell anyone. My parents would get very annoyed and angry when I did not want to visit relatives. If my parents had been a little more aware, my life would not have been plunged into darkness.”

‘Govt must act treating this a national crisis’

Laila Khandakar, convener of the organisation “Shishurai Shob”, told Prothom Alo that the nature of sexual abuse has a lasting impact on children.

Such experiences can interfere with their ability to lead normal lives as they grow older and can affect their relationships with their partners, she said.

“Children need to be taught about inappropriate and appropriate touch to ensure their safety at home, outside and in educational institutions. Arrangements must be made so that children can report abuse to their parents or teachers without fear. The prosecution of accused individuals must be ensured,” she said.

She said sexual abuse of children had reached an alarming level.

“The government must take the lead in preventive measures, treating this as a national crisis,” she said.

item.title: 2 army personnel killed, 1 injured in accident during field firing exercise in Hathazari
item.description:
Two soldiers of the Bangladesh Army have been killed in an accident during a field firing exercise in Hathazari, Chattogram.

An officer has been seriously injured in the incident.

The event occurred today, Wednesday, as informed by the Directorate of Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) in a press release.

The injured officer is being transported to the Combined Military Hospital in Dhaka by helicopter, according to the statement.

The ISPR press release stated, "During a firing exercise today at the Hathazari field firing range in Chattogram, an accident occurred while shelling from a tank, resulting in the deaths of 2 soldiers of the Bangladesh Army and serious injuries to 1 officer."

The statement also mentioned that necessary actions are being taken to investigate the cause of the accident.

item.title: Madrasah teacher beaten, handed over to police over alleged rape of child
item.description:
A madrasah teacher has been accused of raping a girlchild in Sadar upazila of Noakhali. Local residents beat the accused teacher and handed him over to police on Tuesday evening.

The teacher, Mobarak Hossain, also known as Emran, 45, teaches at a local ebtedayee madrasah. The child was a Class-V student at the same madrasah. She also used to receive private tuition from Mobarak Hossain at his home.

The child’s mother filed a case with Sudharam police station under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act in connection with the alleged rape. Mobarak Hossain will be shown arrested in the case and produced before a court Wednesday.

According to police and local residents, the child had become inattentive to her studies and emotionally distressed over the past several months. At one point, she told a family member about the alleged rape. After the news spread, local residents caught Mobarak and beat him before handing him over to police.

Police admitted the injured madrasah teacher to the 250-bed Noakhali General Hospital.

Asked about the incident, Sudharam police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Nazrul Islam told Prothom Alo that preliminary information suggested the child had been raped while receiving private tuition from madrasah teacher Mobarak Hossain.

He said the child would be sent to Noakhali General Hospital for a medical examination. Her mother had filed a case with the police station in connection with the incident, he added.

item.title: Bangladesh braces for 2–3 heatwaves in September
item.description:
Bangladesh is likely to experience a warmer-than-usual September, with the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) forecasting two to three mild to moderate heatwaves across the country during the month.
According to the department’s long-range weather outlook, both daytime and nighttime temperatures are expected to remain above normal, raising the possibility of prolonged periods of hot and uncomfortable weather in several parts of the country.
The outlook was issued following a meeting of the Expert Team on Long-Range Weather Forecasting.
Assistant Meteorologist at the BMD Afruza Sultana said rainfall is likely to remain below normal across all divisions, suggesting that September could be comparatively drier and warmer than usual.
She said the country may experience two to three mild to moderate heatwaves during the month, with temperatures potentially rising to 36–37 degrees Celsius.
According to Sultana, Dhaka, Rajshahi and Khulna divisions are likely to experience the heat more intensely, with the central and western parts of the country expected to be among the areas most affected by the warmer conditions.
“Usually, moisture levels are higher during this time, causing people to sweat more and making it harder for sweat to dry quickly,” she said.
“As a result, people feel more uncomfortable than they do in April, even when temperatures rise above 38°C, because of the higher moisture in the air in September,” she said.
The combination of above-normal temperatures and below-normal rainfall could increase discomfort for residents and put additional pressure on water resources, particularly during prolonged dry spells, she said.
According to the BMD forecast, Dhaka is expected to receive around 260–270 mm of rainfall in September, while Rajshahi may record 240–270 mm and Chattogram 330–360 mm.
Although rain will remain possible, the overall rainfall totals are expected to stay slightly below the respective long-term averages.
Meteorologists have also warned that one to three low-pressure systems could develop over the Bay of Bengal during September. At least one of these systems may strengthen into a monsoon depression, potentially bringing periods of heavy rain to parts of the country.
Despite the overall drier outlook, localized flooding remains a possibility. Rising water levels in major rivers and monsoon rainfall could trigger short-term flooding, particularly in the northern, northeastern and southeastern regions.
Thunderstorms are also expected on around three to five days during the month.
The latest forecast follows a mixed rainfall pattern in August. Chittagong and Mymensingh received above-normal rainfall, while Rajshahi and Rangpur experienced significant rainfall deficits.
Four low-pressure systems formed over the Bay of Bengal during August, with two developing into monsoon depressions that produced heavy rain and thunderstorms.
The highest daily rainfall recorded last month was 198 mm in Hatiya, while the country’s highest temperature reached 37°C in Rajshahi.
With September expected to be comparatively warmer and drier, the BMD has urged residents, farmers and local authorities to remain prepared for heatwaves, water stress and sudden localized flooding as weather conditions evolve.

item.title: Dismissed Ansar member hacked to death in Tangail, 2 arrested
item.description:
A dismissed Ansar member was hacked to death in Basail upazila of Tangail on Tuesday night. Police have arrested two people in connection with the killing.
The deceased was identified as Hanif Khan, 37, son of late Boktar Ali Khan of Habla Uttar Para village in Habla union.
According to police and local residents, miscreants attacked Hanif with sharp weapons while he was returning home from Bilpara Bazar. They hacked him in different parts of his body before fleeing the scene.
Locals later found him and rushed him to Tangail Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival.
ASI Atiqur Rahman, in-charge of the police box at the hospital, said Hanif was brought to the hospital with critical injuries. His body has been kept at the morgue.
Basail police station Officer-in-charge (OC) Alamgir Kabir said Hanif sustained injuries to his hands, legs and head after being hacked with sharp weapons.
Hanif’s wife, Monira Sultana, filed a case over the incident, following which police arrested two people named in the case.
The arrested suspects are scheduled to be produced before a Tangail court on Wednesday.

item.title: Gas supply to remain suspended for 8hrs in parts of Dhaka Thursday
item.description:
Gas supply will remain suspended for eight hours in several areas of Dhaka on Thursday due to pipeline relocation and tie-in work under the Dhaka Elevated Expressway project, Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited said.
According to a notice issued by Titas Gas, the supply will be suspended from 1pm to 9pm on in Basabo, Khilgaon, Madartek, Shahjahanpur, Sipahibagh, Tilpapara, Malibagh, Shantibagh and Taltala Market and adjoining areas.
The interruption is required to facilitate the installation of valves on both sides of the railway tracks at the Shahjahanpur railway crossing and the tie-in work for relocating a distribution pipeline as part of the Dhaka Elevated Expressway project.
The temporary suspension will affect residential and commercial customers in the specified areas.
Titas Gas also said customers in surrounding areas could experience low gas pressure during the work.
The gas distribution company apologised for the temporary inconvenience caused to its customers and other stakeholders.

item.title: Man dies after falling from BIRDEM Hospital building
item.description:
A man died after falling from the roof of the 16-storey BIRDEM Hospital building in Dhaka on Tuesday evening.
The deceased was identified as Dipu Sultan Rasel, 42, son of Imam Uddin and a resident of Rajab Ali Sardar Road in Kadamtali.
Md Nayeem, Sub-Inspector (SI) of Ramna Model Police Station, said Rasel fell from the roof of the building at around 6:15pm.
On receiving information, police rushed to the spot and rescued him.
He was later taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital at around 11:30pm, where the doctor on duty declared him dead upon arrival.
SI Nayeem said the body had been kept at the DMCH morgue for autopsy.
Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident, he added.

item.title: Dhaka ranks third among world's most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka ranked third among the world's most polluted cities on Wednesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 161 at 9:50 am.
The city's air quality was classified as 'unhealthy', meaning people may experience health effects due to elevated levels of air pollutants.
According to the AQI ranking, Malaysia's Kuching topped the list with a score of 184, followed by Kuala Lumpur with 179. Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, ranked fourth with an AQI of 158.
An AQI score between 101 and 150 is considered 'unhealthy for sensitive groups', while readings between 151 and 200 are classified as 'unhealthy'. Scores from 201 to 300 are considered 'very unhealthy', and readings above 301 are categorized as 'hazardous'.
The AQI is used to measure daily air quality and indicate the level of pollution in the atmosphere and its potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, air quality is assessed based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulphur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Bangladesh women thrash Hong Kong China 6-0 to make history in Junior Asia Cup
item.description:
Bangladesh women's hockey team made history at the 2026 Women's Junior Asia Cup Hockey after thrashing Hong Kong China 6-0 in Moki, Inner Mongolia, China, on Wednesday.
The emphatic victory on Chinese soil marked a new milestone for women's hockey in Bangladesh.
With four consecutive victories, Bangladesh emerged as the undefeated champions of the Challengers Group.
Bangladesh began their campaign with a remarkable 7-0 victory over Chinese Taipei before thrashing Pakistan 5-1 and Kazakhstan 4-0 in their next two matches.
The latest victory saw the Tigresses finish the pool stage with a perfect 12 points, setting up a quarterfinal clash against the third-placed team from the Elite Pool.
Bangladesh finished ninth in their maiden Women's Junior Asia Cup appearance in 2024 after losing all their pool matches.
They have now not only improved on their debut finish to guarantee a top-six position, but also become pool champions for the first time and secured their maiden quarterfinal appearance.
At Morin Dawa Stadium in Moki, the Bangladeshi players dominated Hong Kong China from the start, keeping their opponents' defence under constant pressure with wave after wave of attacks.
The breakthrough came in the ninth minute when captain Sharika Rimon put Bangladesh ahead with a brilliant penalty-corner goal.
Airin Akter Ria doubled the lead in the 19th minute with an excellent field goal, while Kona Akter added the third in the 26th minute as Bangladesh ended the first half with a commanding 3-0 lead.
The Tigresses maintained their dominance after the break.
Mosammat Lima scored Bangladesh's fourth goal in the 31st minute, before Airin Ria netted her second and the team's fifth just two minutes later.
Lima completed the rout in the 48th minute with her second goal of the match, sealing a comprehensive 6-0 victory.
Prominent figures from the country's sports community, including officials of the Bangladesh Hockey Federation, extended their congratulations to the team on the historic achievement.

item.title: Record rain forces Asian Games athletes to evacuate accommodation
item.description:
Hundreds of Asian Games athletes in Japan were briefly evacuated from their accommodation as record rainfall lashed host city Nagoya, with competition beginning on Thursday.
Rainwater also leaked into some competition venues, with more wet weather forecast for the coming days.
About 104mm (four inches) of rain fell in an hour in Nagoya on Tuesday, prompting municipal officials to issue an evacuation order for parts of the city.
Scientists say human-induced climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of weather events in Japan and elsewhere.
There is no dedicated athletes' village at this year's Asian Games, with organisers instead relying on a cruise ship, temporary wooden containers and hotels.
An official with Nagoya Port Authority told AFP that "hundreds" of athletes staying at the city's Garden Pier area, where the wooden container huts are located, were told to move to safety.
The athletes returned after the evacuation order was lifted about two hours later.
The Asian Games officially begin with an opening ceremony on September 19 but several events get under way before that.
The basketball competition begins on Thursday.
Rainwater was found in several competition venues but Nagoya Mayor Ichiro Hirosawa said the facilities were not seriously affected and that events would go on as scheduled.
"There has been limited impact like rainwater leaking from the roofs of some buildings, but the situation is not so serious that the opening on the 19th is in jeopardy for now," he said.
"Given the current circumstances, I believe there will be no obstacles to holding the Asian Games."
More than 17,000 athletes and officials are expected at the Games -- a bigger number than the Olympics.
Subway and bus services in Nagoya were temporarily halted on Tuesday and the Japan Meteorological Agency issued its highest flood warning for a major river in the area.

item.title: Real, City open Champions League campaigns with victories
item.description:
Real Madrid and Manchester City began their Champions League campaigns with victories on Tuesday, with Kylian Mbappe and Erling Haaland leading the way for the European heavyweights.
Record 15-time champions Real Madrid defeated Inter Milan 2-1 at the Santiago Bernabeu, while Manchester City, the 2023 champions, secured a 2-0 victory over Porto.
Both clubs are expected to challenge defending champions Paris Saint-Germain this season, with Mbappe and Haaland likely to play key roles in their title bids.
Mbappe opened the scoring after 14 minutes, taking his Champions League tally to 71 goals and moving level with Real Madrid legend Raul in fifth place on the competition's all-time scoring list.
Haaland, meanwhile, scored twice against Porto to take his Champions League total to 59 goals in 59 appearances.
Borussia Dortmund edged Villarreal 3-2, while Real Betis defeated Lille by the same score. Aston Villa also won 3-2 against Club Brugge, and AEK Athens beat LASK 1-0.
Defending champion PSG will begin its title defense on Wednesday against Slovan Bratislava.
Mourinho makes winning return
Jose Mourinho marked his return to Champions League management with a victory as Real Madrid coach, despite Inter enjoying 61% possession.
Madrid took advantage of two costly first-half mistakes by the Italian side.
Inter lost possession deep in its own half, allowing Brahim Diaz to set up Mbappe, who fired a low shot past goalkeeper Josep Martinez.
Martinez was again caught out when Federico Valverde pressured him inside the penalty area and poked the ball into an unguarded net.
Inter reduced the deficit through Carlos Augusto in the 77th minute, setting up a tense closing period.
“There’s so much criticism when a game is boring, but today it was crazy — it could easily have ended 7-6,” Mourinho said.
Mourinho won the Champions League with Inter in 2010 and is seeking a third title as a coach.
Haaland continues scoring form
Haaland maintained his impressive scoring run against Porto, having scored five goals in his previous three matches.
The Norwegian striker finally broke the deadlock two minutes after halftime, heading the ball into the net. He added a second in stoppage time with a side-footed finish to secure City's victory.
The result also maintained new coach Enzo Maresca's perfect start.
“We have to learn. Enzo demands a lot from us and we have to demand a lot from each other,” Haaland said. “We have to win games because at Man City, you have to win trophies.”
Villa end poor start
Aston Villa put their difficult start to the domestic season behind them with a 3-2 victory over Club Brugge in Belgium.
John McGinn scored the opening goal of the Champions League campaign in the 11th minute with a low angled effort.
Brugge equalized through Hugo Vetlesen, but Emiliano Buendia and Nicolas Jackson scored before halftime to give Villa a 3-1 lead.
Nicolo Tresoldi pulled one back from the penalty spot in the 61st minute, but Villa held on.
The victory ended Villa's winless and goalless start to the 2026-27 season following defeats by Brighton and Arsenal and a goalless draw with newly promoted Hull.
Dortmund teenager hospitalized
Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas was taken to hospital after collapsing during his Champions League debut against Villarreal.
The German club said the 25-year-old? [Need correction: Karetsas is a teenager] — teenager had to leave the field because of circulatory problems and was sent to hospital for further tests.
Serhou Guirassy scored twice for Dortmund and also put the ball into his own net as the German side secured a dramatic victory.
Guirassy put Dortmund ahead 2-1 in the 80th minute and converted a penalty five minutes later. Villarreal pulled another goal back through an added-time own goal.
Parrott scores again for Betis
Ireland international Troy Parrott continued his impressive start at Real Betis by scoring the winner in their 3-2 victory over Lille.
Parrott had also scored a late winner against Real Madrid in La Liga on Friday, making his latest goal another decisive contribution for his new club.
AEK Athens secured their win over LASK through Razvan Marin's superb first-half free kick.

item.title: Sabalenka edges Noskova in thriller to keep 3rd straight US Open title bid alive
item.description:
Aryna Sabalenka survived a dramatic battle against Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova on Tuesday, winning 7-6 (7-1), 3-6, 7-6 (10-7) to reach the US Open semifinals and keep her bid for a third consecutive title alive.
The world No. 1 was pushed to the limit by the sixth-seeded Czech before securing victory in a deciding-set match tiebreak.
Sabalenka will next face third-seeded Jessica Pegula, who came from a set down to defeat No. 26 Emma Navarro 3-6, 6-4, 6-3.
Sabalenka defeated Pegula in the 2024 US Open final and also beat her in last year's semifinals after losing the opening set.
The Belarusian sealed Tuesday's quarterfinal with an ace on her second serve, reaching the US Open semifinals for a sixth consecutive year.
Noskova came close to completing an impressive run after winning her maiden Grand Slam title at Wimbledon. She would have become the first woman since Serena Williams in 2016 to follow a grass-court major title by reaching the US Open semifinals.
Sabalenka appeared close to an early exit when Noskova broke in the third set to move 4-2 ahead. But the top seed immediately responded, breaking back at love to level the set at 4-4.
The match went to a deciding tiebreak, where Noskova initially moved ahead 2-0. Sabalenka recovered after a double fault by Noskova gave her a 4-3 lead and then won the next two points to establish control.
Noskova finished with 46 winners and 18 aces, compared with Sabalenka's 42 winners and 12 aces.
Sabalenka had entered the tournament struggling for form on hard courts, losing in the fourth round in both Toronto and Cincinnati. She had also been eliminated at the same stage at Wimbledon.
However, she had not dropped a set before Tuesday's quarterfinal.
The result also kept alive Sabalenka's hopes of retaining the world No. 1 ranking, which she has held for 99 consecutive weeks.
She will lose the top spot if second-ranked Elena Rybakina defeats Zheng Qinwen on Wednesday to reach the semifinals. If Rybakina loses, Sabalenka can retain the ranking by winning the US Open title.
Tiafoe reaches men's semifinals
In the men's quarterfinals, No. 11 seed Frances Tiafoe rallied from two sets down to defeat Alex Michelsen 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6 (10-6).
Tiafoe will meet either defending champion Carlos Alcaraz or eighth-seeded Ben Shelton in the semifinals.
Their quarterfinal began shortly after 11 p.m. following a long day of matches.
Pegula rallies past Navarro
Pegula overcame a slow start against Navarro, who broke her twice in the opening set to take control.
But the third-seeded American recovered in the final stages, winning four consecutive games after Navarro had taken a 2-1 lead in the deciding set.
Pegula's victory set up another US Open meeting with Sabalenka, who will be seeking to maintain her dominance in New York.
For Noskova, the defeat ended her best-ever US Open campaign. Before this year, her best Grand Slam performance was a quarterfinal appearance at the 2024 Australian Open.

item.title: Khaled makes County debut as Hasan goes relentless
item.description:
Bangladesh pacer Khaled Ahmed made his debut in English County cricket today with Kent as his side took on Derbyshire in a crucial game at County Ground, Derby.
His compatriot Hasan Mahmud had already established his as main strike bowler of the Kent, setting a high bar for Bangladesh bowlers.
Hasan struck twice in the opening over against Derbyshire before Khaled messed with Derbyshire middle order on his very first match.
Hasan dismissed Harry Came and Matthew Montgomery in the first over, removing Came caught at slip before trapping Montgomery lbw with a delivery that came in sharply.
The two wickets took Hasan's county tally to 21, underlining his impressive form since making his Kent debut in June.
Hasan had announced himself in county cricket with nine wickets against Lancashire on debut, earning Player of the Match honors as Kent secured a 140-run victory. He added three wickets in his second match and later took seven wickets across two innings against Worcestershire to help Kent to another victory.
His county form came after an impressive Test performance for Bangladesh against Australia in Darwin last month, where he claimed nine wickets in the two innings, including six in the first innings, and was named Player of the Match. Khaled, meanwhile, made an immediate impact on his first appearance for Kent. The Bangladesh international claimed his maiden wicket in his fourth over, trapping Derbyshire opener Muhammad Naeem lbw.
He later dismissed Derbyshire captain Wayne Madsen for 29 to take his wickets tally to two as the opponent reached 122-4 in 39 overs.

item.title: Afghanistan to host multi-format series against Bangladesh and Zimbabwe
item.description:
Afghanistan will host both Bangladesh and Zimbabwe across October and November in an extensive multi-format programme in the United Arab Emirates, featuring a one-off Test, an ODI Tri-Nation Series involving all three sides, and a three-match T20I series and two-match Test series against Zimbabwe.
Proceedings begin with the one-off Test between Afghanistan and Bangladesh from 9-13 October, before all three nations come together for the ODI Tri-Nation Series between 17 and 23 October.
Zimbabwe open their campaign against Bangladesh on 17 October, before facing hosts Afghanistan on 19 October. Afghanistan and Bangladesh then meet in the final league fixture on 21 October, with the top two sides progressing to the final on 23 October.
After the tri-series, Afghanistan and Zimbabwe switch to the shortest format for a three-match T20I series between 27 October and 1 November. The tour then concludes with a two-Test series between the two nations, running from 5-9 November and 13-17 November.
Afghanistan Cricket Board Chief Executive Officer Naseeb Khan welcomed the confirmation of the schedule.
"We are pleased to confirm this important period of international cricket for the Afghanistan National Team," he said. "Playing Bangladesh and Zimbabwe across different formats will provide our players with valuable competitive opportunities and offer our supporters an exciting period of international cricket.
Bangladesh Cricket Board Chief Executive Officer Nizam Uddin Chowdhury was similarly upbeat about the tour ahead, particularly the red-ball assignment.
"The Test match and the tri-nation series promise an exciting period of cricket for fans in both Bangladesh and Afghanistan," he said. "We attach great importance to Tests, and this will be an excellent opportunity for our players to experience red-ball cricket in the UAE for the first time and challenge themselves against a formidable Afghanistan side that has traditionally performed well in these conditions.

item.title: ACC approves charge-sheet against ex-DB chief Harun in two cases
item.description:
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has approved charge-sheets in two cases against former Detective Branch (DB) chief Md Harun-or-Rashid and his brother ABM Shahriar over allegations of acquiring assets beyond their known sources of income and money laundering.
ACC Assistant Director of the Public Relations Department Md Tanzir Ahmed disclosed the information to the media on Wednesday.
According to the ACC, its Dhaka-1 Integrated District Office filed a case against Harun-or-Rashid on December 17, 2024. The investigation found evidence that he had acquired assets worth about Tk21.28 crore. His legitimate income, after deducting expenses, was found to be Tk1,29,15,006. The ACC consequently found evidence of Tk19,98,94,599 in assets acquired beyond his known sources of income.
In another case, Harun-or-Rashid and his brother ABM Shahriar were named as accused. The ACC said it found evidence that Shahriar had acquired Tk18,28,07,555 in assets beyond his known sources of income.
The investigation also found evidence of asset transfers and money laundering. According to the ACC, Shahriar received 1,850 decimals, or approximately 18.5 acres, of land from Harun through a gift deed (heba).
The commission said the cases were investigated by Mohammad Zainal Abedin, deputy director at the ACC headquarters. During the investigation, the authorities reviewed the accused persons’ movable and immovable assets, income tax records and bank transactions.
The ACC said evidence was found not only of acquiring assets beyond known sources of income, but also of concealing the illegal sources of proceeds of crime and laundering money through the transfer, movement and conversion of assets.
Charge-sheets against Harun-or-Rashid were filed under Section 27(1) of the ACC Act, 2004; Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947; and Sections 4(2) and 4(3) of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012.
Shahriar was charged under the same provisions, along with Section 109 of the Penal Code.

item.title: Legal notice seeks mobile network services on Dhaka Metro Rail
item.description:
A legal notice has been sent to Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited (DMTCL), seeking steps to ensure uninterrupted mobile network and call services on metro rail and at stations in Dhaka.
Advocate H M Rashidul Islam Rashed, general secretary of the BUBT Lawyers Association (BULA), sent the notice in the public interest on Wednesday.
Addressed to the managing director of DMTCL, the notice asked the company to allow the country’s 3 major mobile operators — Grameenphone, Banglalink and Robi Axiata (Airtel) — to install mobile network infrastructure in metro rail areas and provide necessary infrastructural facilities.
According to the notice, around 400,000 passengers use the metro rail every day. However, weak or unavailable network services on moving trains and at stations prevent passengers from making emergency calls, while other calls may be disconnected.
The notice requested that necessary steps be taken within 15 days of receiving it and that the sender be informed in writing.
Otherwise, it said legal measures, including filing a writ petition before the High Court in the public interest, would be taken.

item.title: State minister: Dengue outbreak may peak by end of September
item.description:
State Minister for Health and Family Welfare Dr MA Muhit has said the ongoing dengue outbreak may peak in the last week of September and early October.
He made the remarks at a seminar marking World Suicide Prevention Day, organised by the Aachal Foundation and the Human Rights Development Centre, at Dhaka Reporters Unity on Wednesday.
Dr Muhit said dengue cases had started rising again and that the government had launched a three-month campaign to prevent the spread of the disease.
“We are currently facing an urgent public health issue—dengue. Dengue cases have risen again; the increase began yesterday. Two days ago, we predicted that the peak period would arrive in the last week of this month and early October,” he said.
“Prevention is key here. We held a meeting yesterday under the leadership of the prime minister, and we are launching a three-month campaign regarding dengue.”
He said the campaign would involve voluntary organisations and the public, with a focus on dengue prevention, cleanliness drives and raising awareness.
“By involving people and ensuring that everyone looks after their own homes and workplaces, we can protect ourselves, as well as the relatives we live with and the colleagues we work alongside, from dengue,” he said.
He added that the government was also emphasising cleanliness in urban areas as part of its dengue prevention efforts.
Regarding the government’s dengue response, Dr Muhit said there were two main objectives: reducing infections and lowering the mortality rate.
“To achieve this, we—along with the city corporations, Local Government and the Ministry of Health—are working together on prevention, cleaning operations and larvicide application,” he said.
He said steps had also been taken to reduce dengue-related deaths, including refresher training for doctors.
“Working in collaboration with the Society of Medicine, a standard management protocol was developed, and 300 doctors have already received training based on it,” he said.
“Yesterday, we held a meeting with civil surgeons from across the country. We will continue this training programme in every district and upazila nationwide.”
Dr Muhit said dengue outbreaks often cause sudden increases in patient numbers, resulting in shortages of hospital beds, saline and dengue testing kits.
“We began stockpiling supplies two months ago. Based on current trends, we have adequate stocks of dengue test kits and saline. We have also taken measures to ensure this supply chain remains uninterrupted in the future,” he said.
On dedicated dengue beds, he said hospitals had already been instructed to designate beds for dengue patients.
“Should the number of cases rise further, we can increase bed capacity during the peak season,” he said.
“At the same time, we have urged the private sector to step up and play a role during the dengue peak. They must not arbitrarily hike prices during this period and are required to maintain dedicated beds for dengue patients in their facilities.”

item.title: PM: Govt takes measures to prevent project delays, cost increases
item.description:
The government is taking steps to curb repeated extensions in the duration and cost of development projects, as concerns over prolonged implementation and rising expenses persist.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman disclosed the measures on Wednesday in reply to a written question from Comilla-10 lawmaker Md Mobasher Alam Bhuiyan during the question-answer session of the 3rd session of the 13th National Parliament.
The parliamentary session began at 3:30pm with Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram in the chair. At the outset, the prime minister answered written questions.
Tarique said: “The extension of duration and increase in the cost of government development projects in Bangladesh usually do not occur for a single reason. Rather, multiple weaknesses in project formulation, approval, land acquisition, financing, procurement processes and management become interconnected to create this problem.”
He said: “After the government became aware of the tendency to extend project durations and increase costs, various measures have been taken in this regard. These include ensuring accurate feasibility studies before taking up new projects and initiatives to speed up implementation preparations after project approval.”
Work is underway to update the existing guidelines on project formulation, processing, approval and revision, he said. Dashboards are also being established in the relevant ministries and divisions to strengthen monitoring of ongoing projects.
Regular project reviews and close field-level monitoring have also been increased, he said.
Coordination among relevant agencies is being strengthened to expedite land acquisition and utility relocation work.
Instructions have been given to take action under the rules against individuals and organizations responsible for delays after reviewing the reasons for delays, irregularities, increased costs and revisions in projects not completed within the stipulated time, the prime minister said.
“For projects with implementation progress below 30%, the relevant ministries or divisions are taking appropriate measures regarding their restructuring, changes in scope or continuation after considering their utility and effectiveness,” he said.
“In addition, instructions have been given to take up cluster projects under integrated programs instead of taking up projects separately,” he added.
The prime minister also said the use of the electronic government procurement (e-GP) system in government procurement would be expanded.
In appointing project directors, professional qualifications, skills and practical experience will be given the highest priority, while initiatives have been taken to ensure continuity of responsibility where necessary. Work is underway to update the existing policy for this purpose, he said.
Instructions have also been given to prioritize taking up projects under the public-private partnership (PPP) model, Tarique told parliament.
An initiative has also been taken to update the Public Procurement Rules 2025 to make government procurement more competitive and accountable.

item.title: Yemen rebels report fresh Saudi strikes as conflict deepens
item.description:
Yemen’s Houthi rebels reported dozens of Saudi airstrikes on Wednesday as daily attacks continued in a conflict that has reignited during the Middle East war, with hundreds of people killed in fighting near the Red Sea.
More than 40 attacks targeted several regions including the flashpoint areas of Taiz and Hodeida, scene of fierce clashes between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government, the rebels said.
The latest salvos in Yemen’s previously dormant conflict come a day after the Iran-backed Houthis set oil sites ablaze and wounded 73 in their heaviest missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia in years.
The Yemen fighting is taking place against the backdrop of the Middle East war, which erupted in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran.
On Wednesday, Iran said it attacked 20 American vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and targeted a US military base in Jordan in retaliation for US strikes on Iranian oil tankers.
The Middle East war has sucked in Yemen, the energy-rich Gulf and others across the region while roiling the world economy, as oil prices returned to $100 a barrel on Wednesday.
More than 500 people have died since the Houthis launched a major offensive last week to seize territory around the Bab al-Mandab strait, gateway to the Red Sea shipping route.
The rebels, who have been attacking Saudi oil tankers, are trying to tighten their squeeze on the shipments, analysts say -- a lifeline for exports after Iran’s blockade of Hormuz.
Saudi airstrikes targeted “various areas across the governorates of Marib, Al-Jawf, Taiz and Hodeida over the past few hours,” the rebels’ Almasirah TV said on Wednesday.
There was no official comment from Saudi Arabia.
The Saudi civil defense later issued a warning for the southern governorate of Khamis Mushait, near Yemen, but quickly lifted it.
On Tuesday, Saudi authorities vowed to respond to the Houthi attacks, saying they caused fires and temporary shutdowns at oil sites.
The Houthis triggered the return to hostilities in July, when they let an Iranian plane land in defiance of Saudi control of Yemeni airspace.
The government retaliated by striking the airport, an attack the rebels blamed on its sponsor, Saudi Arabia.
The ongoing exchanges risk returning Yemen to a conflict that left hundreds of thousands of people dead and sparked one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises.
The Houthis, after seizing Yemen’s capital and forcing out the internationally recognized government, fought a Saudi-led coalition from 2015 until a United Nations-brokered ceasefire in 2022.
On Tuesday, the European Union urged the Houthis to end their attacks, calling them a “dangerous escalation.”
“We call on the Houthis to immediately end all attacks inside and outside Yemen, including attacks against commercial shipping in the Red Sea,” said Anouar El Anouni, a spokesman for the bloc’s diplomatic service.

item.title: NCC Bank launches Bangla QR service
item.description:
NCC Bank has recently launched Bangla QR services at various selected retail merchant points across the country.
The primary objective of this initiative is to expand the scope of cashless and digital transactions nationwide and ensure easy, fast, and secure payment facilities for customers.
The bank's managing director M Shamsul Arefin inaugurated the service by distributing Bangla QR codes to approximately 200 retail merchants at Sonargaon Janopath Road, the Ceramic Market adjacent to Tongi Chirag Ali Bus Stand, and Savar New Market.
With the launch of this service, small traders, shop owners, and general consumers in those areas will be able to reduce their reliance on cash and make digital payments simply by scanning the QR code.
This will not only make transactions faster and safer but will also preserve a digital record of every transaction.
The inauguration ceremony was attended by Md Habibur Rahman, the bank’s deputy managing director; Mohammad Tariqul Amin, SEVP (corporate banking); AKM Jahidul Alam, EVP & head of operations; Md Jashimuddin, SVP & region head of Outskirt Dhaka; Sharif Mohammad Mahsin, SVP & head of SME; Md Sajjadul Islam, SVP & head of ICT; Md Anisur Rahman Majumder, VP & head of financial inclusion cell; SM Tanvir Hasan, head of retail business unit, DFS Business & Bangla QR, along with other senior officials of the bank.
Through Bangla QR, customers can easily complete payments using any bank or MFS app.
On the other hand, merchants will be able to receive interbank digital payments through a unified QR code.
This will reduce the risks associated with carrying and using cash, while also keeping a digital record of every transaction.
Managing director of NCC Bank M Shamsul Arefin said: "Through the launch of Bangla QR, NCC Bank has established an important milestone in making the country's digital and cashless transaction system more accessible. Bringing small traders and retail merchants into the mainstream of digital transactions is one of our top priorities. Bangla QR is an interbank payment platform where customers can transact seamlessly and securely, and merchants can receive payments from customers of various banks and financial institutions through a common QR system. The launch of this service at Sonargaon Janopath Road, Tongi Market, and Savar New Market reflects the continuity of our digital banking expansion. We will continue our efforts to extend this service to other important commercial and retail markets across the country in the future."

item.title: Nepal Embassy in Dhaka opens donation account for flood victims
item.description:
The Embassy of Nepal in Dhaka has appealed to individuals, organisations and institutions in Bangladesh for voluntary financial contributions to support victims of the devastating August 26 flash floods, opening a dedicated bank account to channel assistance.
The appeal comes after the floods along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers caused widespread loss of life and property, leaving many people injured, missing and severely affected.
The August 26 disaster was triggered after a massive collapse of glacial ice and rock sent debris into the Lhende Khola, unleashing a destructive surge through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems and sweeping through settlements and critical infrastructure downstream.
As of Wednesday, 1,367 bodies had been recovered in Nepal, while 5,132 people remained officially listed as missing, including around 589 foreign tourists, according to Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.
Only 102 of the recovered bodies had so far been identified and handed over to their families.
In a notice issued on September 8 titled “Together for Nepal: An Appeal for Voluntary Contributions to Support Flash Flood Victims,” the embassy said it had received an outpouring of solidarity and offers of assistance from the Bangladesh government, members of the public, institutions and other friends and well-wishers of Nepal.
With inquiries growing over how people in Bangladesh could contribute to the relief effort, the embassy said it had established a dedicated account for voluntary donations.
“We invite interested individuals, organizations and institutions in Bangladesh to join hands with the people of Nepal in this time of need,” the embassy said.
“Every contribution, big or small, will be deeply appreciated.”
According to the notice, contributions can be deposited with Commercial Bank of Ceylon PLC under the account name “Embassy of Nepal, Dhaka,” account number 1000028629, at its Gulshan branch.
The appeal adds a public fundraising channel to the assistance already extended by Bangladesh following the catastrophe.
The Bangladesh government earlier contributed $1 million to the Nepal Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund to support ongoing relief, recovery and humanitarian operations following the floods and landslides.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had also expressed condolences over the loss of life and offered Bangladesh’s assistance to Nepal, while the National Parliament adopted a condolence motion over the disaster.
The Nepal Embassy said the dedicated account was opened specifically in response to increasing requests from Bangladeshis seeking ways to help those affected.
The August 26 disaster caused extensive damage across northern Nepal, destroying homes, roads, bridges and other infrastructure and leaving communities struggling with the consequences of one of the country’s most severe recent natural disasters.
The embassy said those seeking further information about making contributions could contact its designated officials.
The latest appeal now gives individuals and organisations in Bangladesh a direct avenue to join the government-level response and contribute to Nepal’s recovery effort.

item.title: Power, internet restored after fire at Rooppur
item.description:
Electricity and internet connections have been restored following a fire in a room at the Pioneer Base of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Project in Ishwardi, Pabna. Officials said normal operations at the project are continuing.
The fire broke out around 3am on Monday in the server room of the Pioneer Base, damaging several computers, air conditioners, documents, electrical equipment and internet server components.
An Ishwardi Fire Service unit responded and brought the fire under control. Officials said three additional units were also present as part of a routine fire service drill.
Following the fire, electricity supplies to two buildings, including the Pioneer Base, and internet connections to several project offices were temporarily disrupted. The disruption also caused a brief water shortage at the customs building and canteen, but services were later restored.
The fire service initially suspected that an electrical short circuit may have caused the fire. However, the exact cause will be determined after an investigation.
Abu Hashem, the senior station officer on duty at the site, said the fire occurred in a room outside the radiation zone.
“The fire was quickly brought under control, and electricity and internet services are now functioning normally,” he said.

item.title: BB, Al-Arafah Islami Bank sign CMSME working capital refinance fund agreement
item.description:
With the aim of promoting employment generation and the development of the Cottage, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (CMSME) sector, Bangladesh Bank and Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC have signed an agreement worth Tk5,000 crore to ensure working capital financing at affordable profit rates and on easy terms.
Under the revolving refinance scheme, the CMSME Working Capital Refinance Fund, businesses facing difficulties in maintaining their operations due to working capital shortages will be eligible to receive financing at a 9% profit rate.
The agreement signing ceremony was held at the head office of Bangladesh Bank on September 8.
Deputy governor of Bangladesh Bank Md Anis Ur Rahman attended the event as chief guest.
Among others present at the event were executive director of Bangladesh Bank Nahid Rahman, director of SME & Special Programs Department Md Zabdul Islam, additional director Shahanaj Parveen, senior vice president & head of SME business division of Al-Arafah Islami Bank Monirul Islam, and senior assistant vice president & head of agriculture business & refinance unit Sheikh Asadul Haque.
Financing under the refinance fund established by Bangladesh Bank is expected to further accelerate business activities in the CMSME sector, while contributing to increased production, new employment opportunities and greater contribution of the sector to the overall economic activities of the country.

item.title: NRB Bank, BB to offer working capital financing at 9% interest for CMSMEs
item.description:
A participation agreement has been signed between Bangladesh Bank and NRB Bank PLC to disburse loans at low interest rates and on easy terms from the Tk5,000 crore working capital refinance fund for the CMSME sector.
The agreement signing ceremony was held on September 8, at Bangladesh Bank's head office.
Md Zabdul Islam, director of the SME and Special Programs Department (SMESPD) of Bangladesh Bank, and Tarek Reaz Khan, managing director & CEO of NRB Bank PLC, signed the agreement on behalf of their respective institutions.
Md Anis Ur Rahman, deputy governor of Bangladesh Bank, attended the event as chief guest.
Nahid Rahman, executive director of Bangladesh Bank; Shahanaj Pervin, additional director; and Md Aminul Islam, head of the SME Division of NRB Bank PLC, were also present.
Under the Tk60,000 crore stimulus package announced by Bangladesh Bank, this fund was formed to enable CMSME enterprises to operate their production, service, and business activities at full capacity by providing them with the necessary working capital loans/ investments, and to boost the sluggish economy by creating direct and indirect employment in the country.
Under this fund, generally operational CMSME enterprises that are unable to run their production/ service/ business activities at full capacity due to a lack of necessary working capital will receive financing at an interest rate of only 9%.
NRB Bank PLC is a proud partner in this business journey.

item.title: EasyBuy.com.bd launches to simplify product sourcing from China
item.description:
EasyBuy.com.bd, a cross-border wholesale marketplace and sourcing platform, has officially launched with the aim of simplifying product sourcing from China for Bangladeshi entrepreneurs.
The platform was recently unveiled at a grand ceremony held at its corporate office in Elephant Road, Dhaka, under the slogan, “Source Easy, Grow Fast.”
EasyBuy.com.bd will enable entrepreneurs to search for and source a range of products from China at wholesale prices based on their business requirements.
For many aspiring entrepreneurs, students and professionals looking to start online or small-scale businesses, selecting suitable products, identifying suppliers and navigating the sourcing process in China can be challenging.
The platform aims to make these processes more accessible and streamlined.
“Our goal is to simplify the process of sourcing products from China, create new business opportunities for Bangladeshi entrepreneurs and help them grow their businesses,” said Kauser Khandoker, founder and managing director of EasyBuy.com.bd.
Mahsin Ali, co-founder of the company, said the platform seeks to help entrepreneurs source quality products more easily, allowing them to launch and expand their businesses.
EasyBuy.com.bd is an affiliate of Galaxy Cargo International, which has been operating in the China-Bangladesh trade and logistics sector since 2016.
The platform draws on the company's experience in cross-border trade and its network in China to support entrepreneurs throughout the sourcing process.
According to the company, it maintains its own warehouse and office in China, supported by local employees and a dedicated sourcing team that assists customers in identifying and procuring products.
EasyBuy.com.bd aims to serve existing small and medium-sized enterprises, as well as aspiring entrepreneurs, students, professionals and e-commerce businesses seeking easier access to products from China.
